title: Camps C14 — Starts and Ends use the shared time list (6:00 AM–10:00 PM, every 5 minutes)
subtitle: Rule v1.019 (one time list everywhere; camps 6:00 AM–10:00 PM) and v1.109 (the shared components/TimeList.jsx, as drawn in M8). Add / Edit camp → 2. Times → Camp hours. Today Starts and Ends are the browser’s own <select>: 181 times, 6:00 AM–9:00 PM, already every 5 minutes; the list that opens is the browser’s (on phones, the phone’s own picker), so it looks different on every device. After: the shared field and list, the same on every device: every time with AM/PM, ends at 10:00 PM, opens with the chosen time in the middle (tinted, with the 2px blue ring on the row the arrow keys are on), typing a number jumps to that hour. No database change (the camp’s time check only asks for 5-minute steps). Amber = what changes.

The list’s end: 9:00 PM. Drawn: the browser’s open list can’t be photographed, so the real Ends box is shown as a list, scrolled to its last times.

footer: On phones and touch: the list rows are finger-sized (44px), so only about 5 times show at once — 193 times in 5-minute steps is a lot of scrolling by finger; the list opening on the chosen time and typing a number (on a keyboard) to jump to an hour help, but a phone user scrolls. That is the approved v1.109 list, not a Camps choice. On touch the field’s time is 16px but the list’s rows are 13px (measured), so the open list reads smaller than the field it came from — a shared-part detail (M8), noted for Dashboard core, not changed here. On a phone the open Ends list covers the date fields below it and stops just above the pinned Save button (390×844 and 320×700). For the build: TimesSection passes the label’s id (labelId), readOnly while saving, and invalid + describedBy for Camps’ amber line under Ends (“The camp must end after it starts.”); Camps’ own 6:00 AM–9:00 PM list (campForm.js TIME_CHOICES) goes. A saved time outside the list is still shown (the shared list adds it). Drawn: only “Today, the list’s end” (see its caption). The After pictures are the real shared TimeList, mounted over each hidden box with the page’s own React. Script: mock-c14-timelist.js.
